prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The research was a longitudinal study designed to check if total time spent being sedentary links to how the brain's default mode network connects with other areas in young adults.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study included 32 healthy young adults who were part of the Healthy Student Brain project.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers used Fitbit devices to measure the total number of minutes participants spent being sedentary over an eight-week span.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Brain scans were taken while participants rested with their eyes open and with their eyes closed.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Spending more time sedentary was linked to stronger connections between the default mode network and sensory parts of the brain.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The link between sedentary time and visual network connectivity was present whether participants had their eyes open or closed during the scan.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Sedentary time was associated with stronger sensorimotor network connections only when participants rested with their eyes closed, not when their eyes were open.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: No significant links were found between sedentary time and the default mode network's connections to cognitive control, subcortical, cerebellar, or auditory brain regions.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Because the group of participants was small, the authors say the results should be seen as generating ideas for future research rather than proving a fact.
facts.subject: humans
